Siya is a Shark [5886]

By: Carol Albertyn Christie | Delivery

Proposal


Show:

Further information:
Sharks and Siya Proposal

Everyone wants to know exactly what Siya’s move to the Sharks means.
Why did he leave the Stormers? What does the buy out of the Sharks Team mean?

Siya is giving us a one on one interview on Friday.
All of the rugby questions we need to ask we can put to him. Our viewers can suggest questions.

Siya has moved to Sharks as part of agreement between MVM buy out of 51% of Sharks team. Marco Masotti owns MVM Holdings.
We will interview Marco who is an ex South African who grew up in Amanzimtoti. He is a partner at prestigious New York Law Firm Paul Weiss.
And he has now bought 51% of the Sharks Rugby Team under his company MVM Holdings. Buying a sports team is quite an American thing, we will speak to Marco about what this means for South Africa.

https://www.iol.co.za/sunday-tribune/news/rugby-in-the-dna-of-marco-masotti-the-sharks-new-us-investor-bed7f528-5c76-4df9-b387-bf93234e0afc

Initially Marco was inspired by Siya Kolisi’s story and wanted to buy the Stormers in CT. They would not allow him to control the team with a 51% buy in.
He then set sights on Sharks which made more sense as he grew up in KZN and his family lives here.

Part of the Sharks deal was bringing Siya from the Stormers to the Sharks.

Siya has been with the Sharks for a month now and is building form before he goes onto the field again. During lockdown Siya also started the Kolisi Foundation which brought help to communities like the one that he grew up in.
Marco Masotti will also be helping with Siya’s foundation.

Siya is also the first player to be signed to ROC Nation, Jay Z’s company. The CEO Michael Yorman will be in SA on Friday and we can interview him about what this means and creating brands for sports people.

Vincent Mai sponsored Siya to go to Greys in PE. I have requested an interview with him. He remained anonymous until after the World Cup when Siya found out who he was and said to him that this is how his help changed Siya’s life.






Expert:
Mr. Marco Masotti
Mr. Siya Kolisi
Mr. Vincent Mai

Siya Script

V/O
It’s 8 oclock in Durban and the humidity is unbearable. The Sharks team is already honing their skills and practicing drills under the scorching sun. WorldCup Springbok Captain Siya Kolisi is the latest addition to the team.

Siya
“I am just excited to be here. Like I woke up happy this morning . I really want to be here and I want to bring good energy to the guys.”

V/O
It was called rugby’s worst kept secret, Siya Kolisi’s move from the Stormers to the Sharks which was announced at a press conference in February.

Siya
“ People are very welcoming. Amazing people who have called to say welcome. And the Beast was do you want some chicken I‘ll give you wings.”

Upsound

This is Siyamthanda Kolisi 50th test match, Siya is not only a man from the Kolisi family in Zwide, he represents South Africa as a whole.

V/O
First black captain Siya Kolisi and the Springbok team brought elation to millions of South Africans who were cheering them at the 2019 Rugby World Cup.


Siya
“We know we come from different backgrounds and different races, working together with one goal and we wanted to achieve it, I really hope we have done that for South Africa to show that we can achieve anything if we work together as one.”


Link
After winning the world cup Siya Kolisi and having the world at his feet, it’s hard to imagine Siya Kolisi as that young boy from Zwide who didn’t even know where his next meal would come from.

V/O
At times Siya’s grandmother only had sugar water to feed them. Rugby was a distraction from his hunger and this field is where Siya would have played rugby at primary school.







Mac
You were spotted by rugby talent in silk shorts, why were you playing rugby in silk shorts. Lets start there.

Siya
I couldn’t afford. I didn’t have shorts, I couldn’t afford that. It was a trial game and there were three guys from school, made the B team but the school mates were in the A team and Grey wanted them and my teacher from High School said if you take those boys you must take this one too.

V/O
Grey High School is a semi private boy’s school in Gqeberha. Over the years they have produced 14 Springbok Rugby players. Although he was third choice, Kolisi was determined to succeed.

Siya
15 minute drive from the twonship to go to Greys and I walk in and I see the fields and they are like green carpets on what I was used to play in, they were brown with patches of grasss now and then, there are thorns everywhere , we had no shoes and I just saw opportunity and I saw infrastructure to be whatever I want to be. And I walk in that building and my mind set just changedand I knew I have to make this work, no matter what and I will give everything for it.

V/O
Vincent Mai is an ex South African businessman and philanthropist who went to Grey High School and started a scholarship programme for township kids. Over 25 years he has sponsored dozens of young men anonymously.

Vincent
I grew up in Apartheid South Africa and I was the beneficialry as a white South African of a wonderful education but I believe in equal opportunity for everybody.
It has been one of the most fulfilling things in my life. Of course what brings us here that the one in a million chance is named Siya Kolisi.

V/O
At Grey High, Kolisi never knew who sponsored him. After school he spent 11 years in Cape Town. He made his senior debut for Western Province against during the 2011 Vodacom Cup. He became captain for the Stormers in February 2017, the following year he captained the Springboks.


Siya
“I learnt a lot there and I really enjoyed and I grew as a person and also then I started finding my purpose that’s where a lot of my dreams are born. Where I met my wife, my kids, I have so many great memories there and I will always be grateful for the people of Cape Town who welcomed me and my family.”

V/O
In January this year New York lawyer Marco Masotti who heads an international consortium bought a 51% majority stake in The Sharks.
He was born in Amanzimtoti in KZN and is a staunch rugby supporter and believes that with his backing The Sharks could become a global force in the world of rugby.


Marco
“Our vision matches the vision of The Sharks. You know we are coming as shareholders we bring different things to the table but all we are doing is water the flower a little more so that it blossoms and grow. All the seeds are already there. We do have a shared vision we want to win.”

V/O
Masotti has plans to broaden their horizons to play in the Pro 16.

Mac
How will the Sharks fans see the difference?

Marco
They are going to see some exciting talent on the field, they are going to be playing in Europe. So they are going to be playing against different franchises. Hopefully we will have some of the Europeans down at the games and they are going to see the branding of the fan experience in a different way. It will be more than just about rugby at the stadium.

V/O
Vincent Mai also believes that this new partnership is bigger than the sport itsself.

Mai
In another dimension, of how you use not just a great rugby team but how you use a sports franchise to do community outreach to inspire young children for things beyond rugby.

V/O
During lockdown Siya and his wife Rachel started the Kolisi Foundation. They was established it, to change the story of inequality in South Africa. During the pandemic they distributed more than 33 thousand food parcels. And for them this is just the beginning.

Siya
I am still in South Africa, that is what I am grateful for because then I can keep on investing and giving back to the community wherever I go because my story isn’t only down in PE, my story is so many people all around South Africa and that is the thing with the foundation we want to make sure that wherever we go we are making a difference.


V/O
The people who have invested in Masotti’s company, MVM Holdings includes Vincent Mai. Kolisi never knew who paid for his school fees but asked Grey High to release that information when he became a Springbok.

Siya
“I emailed him and I just thanked himfor everything and I sent him a picture of me and my family and I wrote a note at the back and said. The schooling didn’t make me a great rugby player and everything, these are people I have met in my life and are in my life right now, this family wouldn’t have happened without you you know.”

V/O
They met for the first time in New York after the World Cup.

Vincent
“It was one of the most moving experiences I had, because when he got out of the car, and I have to confess I was was tearful.”

Mac
“Who was the first to cry?”

Vincent
“ I was.”

V/O
Vincent Mai and other investors have comitted to supporting the Kolisi Foundation to allow Siya and Rachel to change more people’s narratives.

Siya
You want kids dreams not to be limited and also you need as many reference points as possible. Because now I became a reference point for someone else and say you know what, he did it I can also do it. I have a platform and it has been given to me by the people of South Africa, my family and the hard work and I must make sure I pay it back.”





Promo 1
We know him as the powerhouse who triumphantly held up the rugby world cup trophy. Siya Kolisi grants us personal insights into his journey from Zwide to the The Sharks.



Promo 2
Springbok Siya Kolisi learnt to play rugby on thorny sand fields, but a rugby scholarship lead him to the manicured lawns of Grey High School which changed the trajectory of our rugby history forever.



Promo 3

National hero Siya Kolisi never knew who changed his life who sponsored his schooling at Grey High. Kolisi grants us insights of his remarkable story from Zwide to holding the golden trophy in Japan.
